summary: The cited public historical knowledge records a helper defect that published partial process identity before completing ownership checks. A later readable census could then falsely upgrade unknown cleanup and authorize signaling. The accepted source repair validates ownership facts locally, publishes acquisition atomically, clears incomplete state and makes UNKNOWN sticky. A fully acquired identity remains usable for real cleanup even if writing its receipt fails. The lesson applies to ownership acquisition and cleanup truth; it does not settle the original unknown native operation or authorize cleanup of another process. Recheck applicability before applying it to a successor helper.
title: Publish process ownership atomically and keep failed acquisition unknown
